page: Amazon Web Services trn1n.32xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for distributed machine learning training and deep learning workloads. The platform is powered by 16 AWS Trainium accelerators providing 512 GB of aggregated accelerator memory, paired with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. The host system delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores operating at 3.5 GHz, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 vector support, and 512 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz.

For local data staging and pipeline throughput, the instance integrates 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside 1600 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. In multi-core compute benchmarks, the architecture demonstrates strong throughput, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 86,941.36 and top-tier results in extended instructions and hardware cryptographic operations. Memory caching shows strong performance with read bandwidth reaching 6,684.64 GB/sec for small blocks, complementing multi-threaded decompression rates of 74.17 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge in single-threaded tasks and standalone CPU inference. Both Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core results land in the median range, and CPU-driven text generation on a 70B parameter model yields 2.88 tokens per second. The instance achieves its qualitative cost efficiency when large distributed training jobs actively saturate the 16 AWS Trainium chips and the 1600 Gbps interconnect, rather than running general host CPU workloads.

Amazon Web Services trn1n.32xlarge is best suited for large-scale deep learning model training, distributed natural language processing, generative AI fine-tuning, and high-throughput data ingestion pipelines requiring extensive local NVMe scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services trn1n.32xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built for distributed deep learning and large-scale model training. It is equipped with 16 AWS Trainium accelerators featuring 512 GB of total accelerator memory, paired with 128 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8375C processor, 512 GB of DDR4 system memory, 7600 GB of NVMe SSD local storage, and 1600 Gbps of network bandwidth. In CPU benchmark testing, the host exhibits top-tier multi-threaded cryptographic and vector performance, though single-core execution remains average. The instance delivers high resource density for high-throughput model training, distributed ML clusters, and large data pipelines.
